topic: E-commerce Abandoned Cart WhatsApp Follow-up: 7 Checks Before You Automate
boundary: Educational operations guide only — not legal, privacy, marketing, financial, compliance, certification, savings, ranking, customer-result, approval, or guaranteed-performance advice.

checks.owner_question: Where did the shopper agree to receive WhatsApp, SMS, email, or cart follow-up messages?
checks.safe_action: Keep a visible consent/source note before adding any automated reminder.

checks.owner_question: Is the message useful, or does it feel like a pushy sales chase?
checks.safe_action: Start with one helpful reminder, clear context, and an easy way to stop.

checks.owner_question: When is the cart still relevant without disturbing the buyer?
checks.safe_action: Test a small manual timing window before adding repeated automations.

checks.owner_question: Does the follow-up reference the right item, stock status, delivery concern, or checkout issue?
checks.safe_action: Use product-safe placeholders and avoid guessing reasons the buyer left.

checks.owner_question: Who answers if the buyer replies with a question, complaint, cancellation, or delivery issue?
checks.safe_action: Route replies to an owner before increasing message volume.

checks.owner_question: Will automatic discounts train buyers to abandon carts to get offers?
checks.safe_action: Separate service reminders from discount rules and review margin impact manually.

checks.owner_question: Which messages helped, which annoyed buyers, and which created support work?
checks.safe_action: Track sent count, reply themes, stops/opt-outs, and owner notes before scaling.

safe_scope: Uses consent/source notes, tone review, timing windows, product context, support routing, discount review, and weekly owner evidence review; no customer data, credentials, legal advice, privacy advice, guaranteed revenue, or result claims.
